clue.text: Who had managed to get a seat?

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters have been handled and arranged into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks who succeeded in grabbing a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges WHOHAD; the seat is the kind carried on an elephant's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdah is a canopied seat fixed on the back of an elephant or camel, so it is one kind of seat.

clue.text: Crack I discovered on vessel …

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A fissure found by someone aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' is a wisecrack, not a split; the ellipsis links to the next clue only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack in the sense of a quip is a joke, and a one-liner is a short witty joke.

clue.text: … debris I trusted would be dealt with

indicators.note: dealt with suggests the letters are handled and rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hopes the rubbish found on the ship will be sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would be dealt with' rearranges ITRUSTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is waste matter or rubble, a direct synonym of debris.

clue.text: Carrier claims journalist is outside

indicators.note: is outside means the journalist word wraps around the claims word

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a mediocre one
avers means asserts or claims

explanation.surface: A bag carrier maintains that a reporter is standing outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrier' suggests a person or firm; it is a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A haversack is a bag carried on the back or shoulder, so a carrier in the sense of a bag.

clue.text: Be successful and travel

explanation.surface: Doing well and seeing the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to prosper in a career, and literally means visiting many destinations on journeys.

clue.text: Surprisingly, I never get older right, pet?

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters come out in an unexpected arrangement

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog owner asks their animal if it is true they never age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges INEVERGETOLDER with R.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of dog is a popular family companion, an example of a pet.

clue.text: Got to know writer with the name Edward

parts.note: Edward Lear was a writer of nonsense verse
N is the standard abbreviation for name
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A biography records that the writer bore the name Edward, as Lear did.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to Edward Lear, which is exactly who the writer is.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned is the past tense of learn, which means found out or came to know.

clue.text: Bird seen to turn up at balls

parts.note: to cock is to turn up, as with a hat brim or an ear
taken as written
O is a round letter like a ball, so two give OO

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted raising its head at a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balls' suggests dances; the two Os are round shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatoo is a crested Australian parrot, a type of bird.

clue.text: Take out of the picture subsidiar activity

explanation.surface: Removing an unwanted side business from consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper printed 'subsidiar', a slip for 'subsidiary'; the second definition is a subsidiary activity.
explanation.definitionFit: To sideline someone is to exclude them from action, and a sideline is also a secondary business or hobby.

clue.text: Celebration of summer -——- after start of floods?

indicators.note: after places the summer word behind the opening letter of floods
the start of a word is its opening letter, here of floods

parts.note: estival (aestival) is the adjective meaning of or belonging to summer

explanation.surface: A summer party is held once the rains have begun.
explanation.walkthrough: ESTIVAL, the US spelling of aestival, is a rare word meaning 'of summer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A festival is a gala or celebration, a synonym in everyday use.

clue.text: Turned and fled, pursued by police

indicators.note: pursued by puts the police letters after the fleeing word

parts.note: fled means ran away, so ran
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: A suspect wheeled round and bolted with detectives in chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' is meant as milk going off, not a person turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has turned has gone off, and rancid describes butter or oil that has spoiled.

clue.text: Metalwork, a measure of work I put back in box

indicators.note: in places the reversed pieces inside the box word

parts.note: a box file is a filing container, so file

indicators.note: put back means the work unit and the letter I are read in reverse order

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman stores a piece of metalwork in a box after measuring his effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns ERG + I into IGRE, which sits inside FILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is delicate ornamental work made from fine twisted gold or silver wire, a kind of metalwork.

clue.text: Necessitate English translation of Latin

indicators.note: translation here means the letters are carried over into a different arrangement

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A requirement that English versions of Latin texts be made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' rearranges LATIN into NTAIL, placed after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to involve it as a necessary consequence, so it means necessitate.

clue.text: Girl's brother and I would appear intrepid

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
Fra is the title for an Italian friar, meaning brother
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: A girl says her brother and she would look brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Unafraid and intrepid are synonyms, both meaning fearless.

clue.text: I am one mime who's no good miming

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
I is the Roman numeral for one
Jacques Tati was a French comic actor famed for mime

explanation.surface: A performer confesses to being a hopeless mime artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati was a French film comedian whose humour relied on mime and silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Miming means copying actions without words, just as imitating means copying.

clue.text: God, if upset, would be cross

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so the word for cross is read backwards

parts.note: cross means annoyed or angry, so sore

explanation.surface: A deity would be angry if overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' is an adjective meaning annoyed, not the shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, a specific example of a god.

clue.text: Policeman, about 51, is blocking the way out, that's plain

indicators.note: is blocking means the policeman group stands inside the way-out word

parts.note: an exit is a way out

indicators.note: about means the policeman letters go around the number

parts.note: PC is short for police constable
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A constable stands in the doorway, clearly obstructing the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: PC goes round LI to give PLIC, which then sits inside EXIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit means stated clearly and openly, so plain in meaning.

clue.text: It's publicly known where needle used to be put

definitions.text: where needle used to be put

explanation.surface: A remark officially noted, and where a gramophone stylus sat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means officially stated and public; literally, a gramophone needle rested on a disc.

clue.text: Book featuring schoolboy East

parts.note: Tom Brown is the famous fictional schoolboy of Tom Brown's Schooldays
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A volume starring the schoolboy character East, Tom Brown's friend at Rugby School.
explanation.walkthrough: East really is Tom Brown's friend in Tom Brown's Schooldays, a Victorian novel about life at Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a book, usually a large heavy one.

clue.text: I always get caught by your wrong-doing

indicators.note: get caught by means the pieces are held inside the possessive word

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
taken as written
ever means always

explanation.surface: Someone complains that they are always blamed for the other's misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: I + EVER sits inside THY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thievery is the act of stealing, a particular kind of wrong-doing.

clue.text: Dream about a vehicle in biscuit

indicators.note: about means the dreaming word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to moon is to daydream or idle dreamily
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Daydreaming about a car while eating a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: MOON is a verb here, to moon about; A + CAR sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small almond biscuit or cake.

clue.text: Hoax — it's hard and unpredictable

parts.note: a skit is a send-up or spoof, loosely a hoax
'tis is the old contraction of it is
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A practical joke said to be harsh and erratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' becomes 'TIS, the poetic contraction, rather than being read as ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittish describes a horse or person that is nervous and liable to behave unpredictably.

clue.text: A mediocre build-up for what's his-name

annotationWithheld.why: A mediocre build-up for what's his-name: SO-SO is mediocre, but no clue word gives AND; build-up cannot supply it and indicate insertion at once
annotationWithheld.clue: A mediocre build-up for what's his-name

clue.text: Non-professional receives, on the way back, little room for manoeuvre

indicators.note: receives means the amateur word takes the reversed piece inside it

parts.note: lay means not of a profession, as in a layman

indicators.note: on the way back means the small word is read backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: An amateur driver, reversing, finds he has hardly any space to turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns WEE into EEW, which sits inside LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom or margin to act, the same idea as room for manoeuvre.

clue.text: Ready as I can be made, probably

indicators.note: can be made suggests the letters can be fashioned into something new

parts.note: the fodder letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are as prepared as possible, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made' rearranges READYASI.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedge used to mean I suppose or very likely, so it stands for probably.

clue.text: It's unclear how stupid fellow grasps university year

indicators.note: grasps means the dolt word holds the university letter inside

parts.note: a clod is a dull, stupid person

explanation.surface: It is puzzling how a dim student manages a year at college.
explanation.walkthrough: U sits inside CLOD, then Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloudy means murky or not clear, as of a liquid or a meaning.

clue.text: Organ, very old and cooler

parts.note: an icebox is a cooler for keeping food cold

explanation.surface: A very old keyboard instrument stored with a cold box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests a church instrument; it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The larynx, colloquially called the voice box, is an organ of the throat.

clue.text: Help out with season finished

parts.note: tide is an old word for season, as in Yuletide
over means ended or finished

explanation.surface: Assistance given once the holiday period has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To tide someone over is to help them through a difficult spell, so it means help out.

clue.text: Country man has a fund of reminiscences

parts.note: guy is informal for a man
ana is a collection of anecdotes or reminiscences about a person

explanation.surface: A rural fellow owns a store of memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' reads like rural, but it is the definition; ANA is crossword-friendly vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is a nation on the north coast of South America.
